report.answer_text:
Cause
The outage began in AWS's US-EAST-1 region in Northern Virginia and was not a cyberattack. It was a fault inside AWS itself.[1]
Trigger: AWS's post-incident report said the root cause was a latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management system.[2] The system has a "Planner" that decides what changes to make and an "Enactor" that applies them.[3] A race condition let an older version overwrite a newer one, which left the DNS records inconsistent.[3]
Result: The automation left the DynamoDB address record empty, so anything trying to reach DynamoDB in that region couldn't find it.[1]
Cascade: Services that depend on DynamoDB also began failing, including the system that launches new servers and the load balancers that spread traffic.[1] DynamoDB was reachable again by 2:40 AM Pacific on Monday. The knock-on problems with launching servers and load balancers lasted until 2:20 PM Pacific that afternoon.[1]
Aftermath: AWS disabled the DNS Planner and Enactor automation worldwide while it added safeguards.[4]
Timeline
AWS's own summary puts the start at 11:48 PM Pacific on Sunday, October 19.[1] By 3:01 PM PDT on October 20, AWS announced that all services had returned to normal.[5]
What it disrupted
Amazon's own services: Amazon.com went dark, along with several Amazon subsidiary services and AWS customer support operations.[5] Alexa requests such as asking for the weather or turning off lights failed too.[6] Ring was also affected.
Social and communication apps: Zoom and Slack were hit.[7] Snapchat was among the most visible casualties, and Reddit was also affected.
Finance: Coinbase, Venmo and Robinhood were among the services with problems.[8] In the UK, Lloyds Bank, Halifax, Bank of Scotland and HM Revenue & Customs were affected.[7]
Gaming: Fortnite, Wordle and Roblox were affected.[9]
Streaming and media: Disney+, Prime Video and Hulu were hit.[10]
Other sectors: Banks, airlines, media, delivery apps and many other websites and apps were affected.[11]
The outage lasted several hours and affected over 1,000 businesses.[7] It showed how many services depend on a single AWS region.
